title_en: Chongqing Construction Engineering Group Co., Ltd. v. China Railway 19th Bureau Group Co., Ltd. — dispute over construction project contract
ruling_gist_en: 1. According to the Audit Law, the audit conducted by a state audit authority on a construction entity is an act of administrative supervision. The legal relationship arising from the state audit between the auditor and the auditee is different in nature from the civil legal relationship between the parties in this case. Therefore, in a civil contract, the parties' agreement to accept administrative audit as a basis for determining civil legal relationships should be clear and specific, and it should not be inferred through interpretation or presumption that at the time of contract formation, the parties had already agreed to accept the intervention of the state authority's audit into the civil legal relationship.

full_text_en:
Chongqing Construction Engineering Group Co., Ltd. v. China Railway 19th Bureau Group Co., Ltd. — dispute over construction project contract

【Ruling Summary】

I. According to the provisions of the Audit Law, the audit conducted by state audit authorities on construction project entities is an administrative supervisory act. The legal relationship arising from state audits between the audit authority and the auditee is different in nature from the civil legal relationship between the parties in this case. Therefore, in a civil contract, the parties' agreement to accept administrative audit as the basis for determining civil legal relations must be specific and explicit, and cannot be inferred through interpretation that at the time of contract signing, the parties had already consented to the intervention of state audit conduct in the civil legal relationship.

II. Where the parties have confirmed the final settlement price of the project through a settlement agreement and have substantially performed it, the audit report issued by the state audit authority shall not affect the validity of the settlement agreement between the parties.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court
(2012) Min Ti Zi No. 205

Applicant for Retrial (Defendant at First Instance, Counterclaim Plaintiff, Appellant at Second Instance): China Railway 19th Bureau Group Co., Ltd., domiciled at Building 1, No. 19 Ronghua South Road, Beijing Economic-Technological Development Area, Beijing.
Legal Representative: Ge Yongli, Chairman of the Board.
Agent ad litem: Deng Qun, lawyer of Beijing Dongyuan Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Zhang Siqi, female, 2011 graduate student of Renmin University of China Law School, domiciled at No. 59 Zhongguancun Street, Haidian District, Beijing.

Respondent (Plaintiff at First Instance, Counterclaim Defendant, Appellee at Second Instance): Chongqing Construction Engineering Group Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 1596 Jinkai Avenue, North District, Chongqing Economic and Technological Development Zone.
Legal Representative: Yang Jingpu, Chairman of the Board.
Agent ad litem: Zhang Zhaoxin, lawyer of Beijing Dongyi Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Sun Jing, lawyer of Beijing Hanzhuo Law Firm.

The applicant for retrial, China Railway 19th Bureau Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter China Railway 19th Bureau), and the respondent, Chongqing Construction Engineering Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter Chongqing Construction Engineering Group), disputed over a construction project contract. The Chongqing High People's Court rendered Civil Judgment (2012) Yu Gao Fa Min Zhong Zi No. 00006 on March 19, 2012. China Railway 19th Bureau, dissatisfied with the judgment, applied to this Court for retrial. This Court rendered Civil Ruling (2012) Min Shen Zi No. 830 on August 27, 2012, ordering a retrial of this case. This Court lawfully formed a collegial panel and held a hearing on January 15, 2013. The agents ad litem of China Railway 19th Bureau, Deng Qun and Zhang Siqi, and the agents ad litem of Chongqing Construction Engineering Group, Zhang Zhaoxin and Sun Jing, appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. The trial of this case has now concluded.

The facts found by the Chongqing No. 1 Intermediate People's Court (hereinafter Chongqing No. 1 Intermediate Court) at the first instance are as follows:

On August 22, 2003, Chongqing Jinkai Industrial Co., Ltd. (hereinafter Jinkai Company), as the project owner and supervisory unit of the Jinshan Avenue West Extension Road Project in the Jingkai Park of the New North Zone of Chongqing, entered into a Construction Project Construction Contract for the Jinshan Avenue West Extension Road Project with Chongqing Construction Engineering Group, awarding the project to Chongqing Construction Engineering Group. In the Pricing Principles for the Project Cost of the Jinshan Avenue West Extension Road Project, the parties agreed on the determination of prices for unpriced materials, special materials for overpasses, and unpriced materials for street lamps as follows: "to be determined by the Jinkai Company and the Jingkai District Supervision and Audit Bureau and incorporated into the project settlement." China Railway 19th Bureau was confirmed by Jinkai Company as the subcontractor for the Lanfeng Tunnel Project and entered into a Single Project Subcontract (hereinafter subcontract) with Chongqing Construction Engineering Group on November 17, 2003. The main terms provided that Chongqing Construction Engineering Group subcontracted the Lanfeng Tunnel Project of the Jinshan Avenue West Extension to China Railway 19th Bureau, with a tentative contract price of RMB 80,000,000 (final settlement price subject to the owner's audit). Article 6.2 on fund management stipulated: after the project is completed, passes comprehensive acceptance inspection, and the settlement is reviewed and determined by the audit department, the remaining project tail payments shall be paid upon the deduction of the project warranty bond, and the parties shall separately enter into a supplementary agreement to specify. The contract also provided specific terms on project content, contracting and settlement, etc. Thereafter, China Railway 19th Bureau performed the construction in accordance with the contract.

In December 2003, Jinkai Company underwent restructuring, and the project owner of the Jinshan Avenue West Extension Road Project in the Jingkai Park of the New North Zone of Chongqing was changed to the Chongqing Economic Development Zone Land Reserve and Renovation Center, i.e., the current Chongqing New North Zone Land Reserve and Renovation Center (hereinafter Land Reserve Center). In 2005, Jinshan Avenue was renamed Jinyu Avenue.

On September 8, 2005, the Jinshan Avenue West Extension Road Project was completed, passed acceptance inspection in December of the same year, and obtained the Chongqing Construction Project Completion Acceptance Filing Registration Certificate (Jian Jun Bei Zi [2006] No. 024) on February 6, 2006. Thereafter, for the purpose of providing a value basis for the completion settlement of the Lanfeng Tunnel and Huagou Tunnel sections of this road project, the Chongqing Economic Development Zone Supervision and Audit Bureau (hereinafter Jingkai District Supervision and Audit Bureau) commissioned Chongqing Xiheng Bidding Agency Co., Ltd. (hereinafter Xiheng Company) to conduct a completion settlement audit for the above projects. On August 10, 2006, Xiheng Company issued the Basic Construction Project Settlement Audit Report (hereinafter Audit Report), stating that the cost of the Lanfeng Tunnel was RMB 114,281,365.38 (including RMB 28,569.53 for the sidewalk surface layer inside the Lanfeng Tunnel, which is not part of the disputed project scope). Based on this Audit Report, Chongqing Construction Engineering Group and China Railway 19th Bureau on December 5, 2007, carried out a settlement for the subcontracted project of China Railway 19th Bureau, confirming that the settlement amount within the drawing scope for China Railway 19th Bureau was RMB 114,252,795.85. After deducting various fees, the subcontract settlement amount was RMB 102,393,794 (taxes and other fees to be collected by the financial department according to regulations). As of the time of the first instance lawsuit, Chongqing Construction Engineering Group had cumulatively paid China Railway 19th Bureau RMB 98,120,156.63 in project funds for the project in question.

From October 9 to November 21, 2008, the Chongqing Audit Bureau, with the Land Reserve Center as the auditee, conducted a completion settlement audit for the Jinyu Avenue (formerly Jinshan Avenue) Road Project and issued the Audit Report Yu Shen Bao [2008] No. 142, determining that the Land Reserve Center should reduce the completion settlement price of the project by RMB 15,481,440.93, including a reduction of RMB 8,168,328.52 for the Lanfeng Tunnel project in question based on the submitted amount of RMB 114,252,795.85. On December 24 of the same year, the Chongqing Audit Bureau issued the Audit Decision on the Completion Settlement of the Jinyu Avenue Road Project in Jingkai Park of the New North Zone (Yu Shen Jue [2008] No. 111), ordering the Land Reserve Center to reduce the settlement price of the project by RMB 15,481,440.93, adjust relevant accounts, and required the Land Reserve Center to implement the decision before March 20, 2009.

On February 9, 2009, the Land Reserve Center issued a letter to Chongqing Construction Engineering Group, Letter on Implementing the Audit Decision of the Chongqing Audit Bureau on the Completion Settlement of the Jinyu Avenue (Former Jinshan Avenue) Project (Yu Xin Tu Chu Han [2009] No. 5), requiring it to refund the reduced amount to the Land Reserve Center before March 1, based on the reconsideration result of the Chongqing Audit Bureau. Chongqing Construction Engineering Group has already deducted and returned part of the funds.

On September 1, 2010, Chongqing Construction Engineering Group filed a lawsuit with the Chongqing No. 1 Intermediate Court, alleging that based on the audit of the Jinshan Avenue West Extension Project by the Chongqing Audit Bureau, the price for the work completed by China Railway 19th Bureau was reduced by RMB 8,168,328.52. After deducting the fees agreed by the parties, the actual subcontract settlement amount should be RMB 94,878,931.76 (including the management fee to be refunded by Chongqing Construction Engineering Group). Chongqing Construction Engineering Group had cumulatively paid China Railway 19th Bureau RMB 98,120,156.63 in project funds before the above audit, overpaying by RMB 3,241,224.87. Therefore, it requested: 1. China Railway 19th Bureau immediately return the overpaid project funds of RMB 3,241,224.87 to Chongqing Construction Engineering Group; 2. China Railway 19th Bureau bear the litigation costs of this case.

China Railway 19th Bureau argued and counterclaimed: The Jingkai District Supervision and Audit Bureau was the competent audit body for this project. After the project was completed, in accordance with the subcontract agreement, the Jingkai District Supervision and Audit Bureau, for the purpose of providing a basis for the completion settlement of the project in question, commissioned Xiheng Company to conduct a cost audit. The Audit Report issued by Xiheng Company was recognized by the project owner, Chongqing Construction Engineering Group, and China Railway 19th Bureau, consistent with the subcontract agreement's provision that "the final settlement price shall be subject to the owner's audit." Based on Xiheng Company's report, Chongqing Construction Engineering Group and China Railway 19th Bureau entered into a subcontract settlement agreement, which was lawfully established, legally valid, and binding on both parties. Both parties had substantially performed under this agreement. The audit by the Chongqing Audit Bureau was a secondary audit, not within the scope agreed by the parties in the subcontract. It could not deny the validity of the Xiheng Company Audit Report, nor was it recognized by China Railway 19th Bureau. Its audit report and conclusions were not binding on the parties to this case and did not affect the validity of the subcontract settlement agreement. Based on the relativity of contracts, Chongqing Construction Engineering Group's negotiation with the owner to change or adjust the total contract settlement price based on the audit report and audit decision of the Chongqing Audit Bureau was not binding on China Railway 19th Bureau, which received the subcontract settlement price according to the subcontract agreement. Chongqing Construction Engineering Group still owed China Railway 19th Bureau RMB 4,273,637.37 in project funds that had not been paid. Therefore, it requested the rejection of all claims of Chongqing Construction Engineering Group and counterclaimed: 1. Chongqing Construction Engineering Group immediately pay China Railway 19th Bureau the overdue project funds of RMB 4,273,637.37; 2. Chongqing Construction Engineering Group pay China Railway 19th Bureau the loss of capital occupation for the overdue project funds, calculated at the bank loan interest rate for the same period, from June 6, 2009, until the date of payment; 3. Chongqing Construction Engineering Group bear all litigation costs of this case.

Chongqing Construction Engineering Group replied to the counterclaim, arguing that the parties had agreed to take the final audit result as the basis for settlement. The settlement agreement signed on December 5, 2007, could not serve as the final settlement basis for this project. Xiheng Company was not the audit unit agreed by the parties, and its audit report was not the final audit report agreed by the parties. Therefore, the report issued by Xiheng Company could not be used as the audit basis for the parties' settlement. It requested the rejection of China Railway 19th Bureau's counterclaim.

The Chongqing No. 1 Intermediate Court held at the first instance that after Chongqing Construction Engineering Group contracted the Jinshan Avenue West Extension Road Project from the construction unit Jinkai Company, with Jinkai Company's consent, it subcontracted the Lanfeng Tunnel project to China Railway 19th Bureau. This did not violate the mandatory provisions of laws and administrative regulations, was legally valid, and the subcontract agreement signed by the parties was binding on both sides. Both parties should perform according to the contract. The main issue in dispute was the determination of the settlement basis for the project involved, namely whether Xiheng Company was the audit unit conforming to the contract agreement, and whether the project settlement should follow the amount confirmed by the parties on December 5, 2007, or the amount determined by the audit report of the Chongqing Audit Bureau. According to the Audit Law and the relevant provisions of the Chongqing Municipality National Construction Project Audit Measures, the project involved was a municipal key construction project in Chongqing, and its completion settlement should be audited by the Chongqing Audit Bureau. The Jingkai District Supervision and Audit Bureau, as an internal audit institution of the Jingkai District, was not a state audit authority and had no authority to exercise audit supervision on behalf of the state. The agreement on the contract price in the subcontract agreement between the parties did not specify whether the audit referred to the internal audit of the audited unit or the audit by the state audit authority, and it could not be inferred that the audit agreed by the parties was internal audit. In this case, the Audit Report issued by Xiheng Company upon the entrustment of the Jingkai District Supervision and Audit Bureau was issued in the name of Xiheng Company. Even if the Jingkai District Supervision and Audit Bureau recognized the audit result, it could not be concluded that the Audit Report had the nature of an internal audit conclusion and decision. The Jingkai District Supervision and Audit Bureau was neither a state audit authority with jurisdiction over the project under the law, nor was the Audit Report issued by Xiheng Company an audit result. China Railway 19th Bureau's assertion that the Jingkai District Supervision and Audit Bureau was the competent audit body and Xiheng Company was the audit unit conforming to the parties' agreement was unfounded. Since the audit jurisdiction over the project belonged to the Chongqing Audit Bureau, its completion settlement audit of the project was an act of exercising state audit supervision according to law, and there was no repeated audit. Its audit decision had a certain compulsory force, and the audited unit and relevant assisting execution departments or units should proactively implement or assist in its implementation. Although audit was an administrative supervision by the state over the construction unit and did not itself affect the validity of contracts between civil subjects, the parties' agreement in this case that "the final settlement price shall be subject to the owner's audit" effectively meant taking the audit result of the audit authority with audit jurisdiction over the owner as the final basis for the parties' settlement. Considering the fact that the Land Reserve Center required Chongqing Construction Engineering Group to refund the reduced amount based on the reconsideration result of the Chongqing Audit Bureau, it proved that the owner ultimately recognized and implemented the amount determined by the Chongqing Audit Bureau's audit report. Based on the parties' contract agreement in this case, the relevant provisions on budget management of government investment and projects mainly funded by government investment, and the specific circumstances of this project, the Audit Report issued by Xiheng Company upon entrustment by the Jingkai District Supervision and Audit Bureau only provided a temporary basis for the settlement of this project. The actions of the parties in this case, such as confirming the total project price as RMB 102,393,794 based on the Audit Report and Chongqing Construction Engineering Group paying part of the funds according to the above settlement, were only interim actions in the settlement process of the disputed project and could not be used to oppose the contract agreement between the parties on project settlement and the relevant laws and regulations on audit supervision. Therefore, China Railway 19th Bureau's claim that Chongqing Construction Engineering Group should pay the outstanding project funds and interest based on the settlement conducted on December 5, 2007, was unfounded and was not supported by the court. Chongqing Construction Engineering Group's claim for China Railway 19th Bureau to return the overpaid project funds was legally grounded and was supported by the court.

The Chongqing No. 1 Intermediate Court, in accordance with Articles 4 and 92 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the judgment: 1. China Railway 19th Bureau shall, within ten days after the judgment takes effect, return to Chongqing Construction Engineering Group the overpaid project funds of RMB 3,130,595; 2. Reject the other claims of Chongqing Construction Engineering Group; 3. Reject the counterclaims of China Railway 19th Bureau. The court acceptance fee for the main action was RMB 32,729.80, of which Chongqing Construction Engineering Group bore RMB 1,117.80 and China Railway 19th Bureau bore RMB 31,612; the court acceptance fee for the counterclaim was RMB 20,495, borne by China Railway 19th Bureau.

China Railway 19th Bureau, dissatisfied with the judgment of first instance, appealed to the Chongqing High People's Court (hereinafter Chongqing High Court), arguing that the subcontract agreement only provided that the "audit" of the owner on the subcontract project was a prerequisite for final settlement, without any restrictions on the handling unit, specific implementation method, or form of audit conclusion. This clause should be interpreted as meaning that any audit result recognized by the owner would suffice as the basis for project settlement. After the Jingkai District Supervision and Audit Bureau commissioned Xiheng Company to audit the project settlement, the project owner Land Reserve Center signed and sealed on the Audit Report, indicating its recognition of both the entrustment of Xiheng Company for audit and the Audit Report itself. The Audit Report conformed to the "owner's audit" as agreed in the contract, and the conditions for settlement under the contract were met. The settlement agreement signed on December 5, 2007, constituted the final settlement act for the subcontract project. The audit by the Chongqing Audit Bureau on the Land Reserve Center was an administrative act initiated ex officio, an ex post supervision over the Land Reserve Center. The counterparty in this administrative legal relationship was the Land Reserve Center, and it could not deny the legality and legitimacy of the performance acts in the civil legal relationship between the parties in this case. Chongqing Construction Engineering Group's agreement to return the reduced amount to the Land Reserve Center was a new mutual agreement reached between Chongqing Construction Engineering Group and the Land Reserve Center beyond the already performed acts. However, there was no mutual agreement between Chongqing Construction Engineering Group and China Railway 19th Bureau to modify the settlement based on the Chongqing Audit Bureau's audit result. China Railway 19th Bureau had no opportunity to raise objections to the Chongqing Audit Bureau's audit report. If the audit result directly took effect against China Railway 19th Bureau, it would constitute improper infringement of legitimate civil rights by administrative power. Therefore, the audit report of the Chongqing Audit Bureau and its demand for the Land Reserve Center to reduce the project funds did not automatically have legal effect on China Railway 19th Bureau. Hence, it requested: 1. Set aside the first instance judgment; 2. Amend the judgment to reject all claims of Chongqing Construction Engineering Group and uphold all counterclaims of China Railway 19th Bureau.

Chongqing Construction Engineering Group replied, arguing that although the parties were not the counterparties of the Chongqing Audit Bureau's audit, the agreement that the final audit result of the owner would be the basis for settlement was explicitly provided in the contract. Therefore, the owner's ultimate determination that the audit result of the Chongqing Audit Bureau would serve as the basis for settlement did not violate the parties' agreement. Although the owner signed on the Audit Report, that report was not the final determination and did not meet the settlement conditions agreed in the contract, and could not be used as the settlement basis. The project in question was a key project invested by the government. The owner could not be the audit subject; it could only be the audit object. The "audit department" as agreed in the contract was itself a legal concept, referring specifically to the Audit Bureau; no other organ could replace it. The first instance judgment found the facts clearly and applied the law correctly. It requested the dismissal of the appeal and affirmation of the original judgment.

The facts found by the Chongqing High Court at the second instance are consistent with the facts found at the first instance.

Chongqing High People's Court found at second instance that the focus of the dispute in this case is whether the project should use the review report issued by Xiheng Company commissioned by the EDZ Supervision and Audit Bureau or the audit report issued by the Chongqing Municipal Audit Bureau as the basis for settlement. The subcontract signed by China Railway 19th Bureau Group Co., Ltd. and Chongqing Construction Engineering Group Co., Ltd. represented the true intentions of both parties. Moreover, the matters subcontracted were also approved by the proprietor and did not violate mandatory provisions of laws or administrative regulations. Therefore, the first instance judgment's finding that the subcontract is valid is correct. The parties agreed in the contract that "the final settlement price shall be subject to the proprietor's audit." The term "audit" itself has its specific meaning. Whether it can be expansively interpreted should be analyzed in light of the actual circumstances of the project involved and the true purpose of the parties in making such an agreement. The project in question is a key project invested by the government and should be subject to state audit supervision. That is, the financial revenues and expenditures of the project proprietor must be bound by such audit supervision, and such audit supervision is not necessarily subject to the will of the proprietor or the parties. The parties in this case were aware of this. The parties' agreement in the contract to take the audit by a third party independent of both parties as the basis for settlement fully demonstrates that they knew that such an audit is strict and important and would affect the final settlement results of both parties and the proprietor. Based on this, the term "audit" agreed in the contract should be restrictively interpreted as a statutory audit, not a broad review. From the perspective of the subject qualification for audit, the proprietor of the project in question is not an audit department or audit organ, does not have the qualification to be an audit subject, cannot become an audit subject, and cannot complete the audit act. In this case, neither the issuer nor the entrusting party of the review report or the audit report is the proprietor. Therefore, the contract does not limit the audit subject to the proprietor. The audit subject for the project in question should follow the statutory audit subject. According to the Audit Law of the PRC and the Chongqing Municipal Measures for the Audit of National Construction Projects, as a municipal-level key construction project of Chongqing, the statutory audit subject for the project in question is the Chongqing Municipal Audit Bureau. The EDZ Supervision and Audit Bureau, as an internal audit institution of the EDZ, is not a statutory state audit organ and cannot exercise audit supervision functions on behalf of the state over the project in question. Therefore, the Chongqing Municipal Audit Bureau is the audit subject that conforms to the contract, and the audit results it issues are the settlement basis that conforms to the contract of both parties. Moreover, even if interpreted according to China Railway 19th Bureau's assertion that "proprietor's audit" means "audit approved by the proprietor," the audit ultimately approved and recognized by the proprietor is still the audit conclusion of the Chongqing Municipal Audit Bureau. The review report is only a stage review opinion during the construction process, not the final audit result. Since the project audit had not yet been completed at that time, the settlement made by the parties based on the review report was only a stage act in the settlement process between the parties, not the final settlement. The final settlement between the parties still depended on the formation of audit results that conform to the contract. However, the agreement reached by the parties on the calculation method of other expenses during the settlement is valid and still binding on both parties. Therefore, the first instance court's calculation of the final settlement amount between the parties based on the audit results of the Chongqing Municipal Audit Bureau and the calculation method of other expenses undisputed by both parties was not improper. Audit, as a form of administrative supervision by the state, generally does not directly produce legal consequences for the settlement of the parties unless the parties have agreed to use audit results as the basis for settlement. However, in the case where both parties have voluntarily chosen to use audit results to bind their settlement, although it formally appears as interference of administrative power in civil legal relations, this is precisely a manifestation of the parties' autonomy of will. In this case, the parties clearly agreed in the contract to use audit as the basis for settlement. The parties knew or should have known and must accept the possible consequences. Therefore, the appeal request of China Railway 19th Bureau lacks factual and legal basis.

The Chongqing High People's Court, in accordance with Article 153, paragraph 1, item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, rendered the following judgment: the appeal is dismissed and the original judgment is affirmed. The second instance case acceptance fee of RMB 77,800 is to be borne by China Railway 19th Bureau Group Co., Ltd.

Dissatisfied with the second instance judgment, China Railway 19th Bureau Group Co., Ltd. applied to this Court for retrial, claiming that the settlement agreement signed between China Railway 19th Bureau and Chongqing Construction Engineering Group was the true expression of the parties' intentions, its content did not violate national laws, and it was legal and valid. According to the Contract Law and relevant judicial interpretations, state audit cannot negate a settlement agreement already reached between the parties. Neither the first instance nor the second instance judgment canceled the settlement agreement or found it invalid, and Chongqing Construction Engineering Group did not request the cancellation or invalidation of the settlement agreement. Therefore, using the audit report of the Chongqing Municipal Audit Bureau to negate the validity of the settlement agreement lacks factual and legal basis. The legal effect of the settlement agreement is the same as that of the subcontract. The first and second instance judgments' invalidation of the settlement agreement based on the understanding of the subcontract terms has no legal basis. The first and second instance judgments confused Xiheng Company's social audit with the internal audit of the EDZ Supervision and Audit Bureau, which is a basic conceptual error. Using reasons such as the EDZ Supervision and Audit Bureau violating the principle of audit jurisdiction and the invalidity of internal audit to invalidate the settlement agreement by implication is contrary to the principle of party autonomy under the Contract Law. State audit cannot negate the validity of social audit. The parties in this case did not agree on state audit, social audit does not belong to internal audit, and there is no issue of so-called audit jurisdiction. Therefore, the application requests: 1. To set aside the Chongqing High People's Court (2012) Yu Gao Fa Min Zhong Zi No. 00006 civil judgment and the Chongqing No. 1 Intermediate People's Court (2010) Yu Yi Zhong Fa Min Chu Zi No. 425 civil judgment; 2. To dismiss all claims of Chongqing Construction Engineering Group; 3. To amend the judgment to order Chongqing Construction Engineering Group to pay China Railway 19th Bureau the arrears of project funds of RMB 4,273,637.37 plus interest calculated at the loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the same period from June 6, 2009, to the date of actual payment.

In its retrial defense, Chongqing Construction Engineering Group argued that the review report issued by Xiheng Company is not a social audit report, as Xiheng Company does not have the qualification to conduct social audits. That report is merely a stage review opinion. The EDZ Supervision and Audit Bureau is an internal department of the EDZ and does not have the qualification to be an audit subject. The review report is only an internal review and cannot replace the final completed project settlement audit. The audit report issued by the Chongqing Municipal Audit Bureau is the basis for the final settlement of the project between the parties. Because the disputed project is a key construction project determined by Chongqing Municipality, it falls within the scope of statutory audit and must be subject to state audit supervision. The parties stipulated in the subcontract that the final settlement price shall be subject to the proprietor's audit, which clearly provides that the audit is the final settlement basis. According to the opinion of the Supreme People's Court's telephone reply, this situation should be considered as the parties having agreed to take the state audit as the settlement basis. The audit report of the Chongqing Municipal Audit Bureau is binding on the proprietor of the project, Chongqing Construction Engineering Group, and China Railway 19th Bureau. During the enforcement process in this case, the parties have already reached a settlement agreement in enforcement, and China Railway 19th Bureau has substantially completed its payment obligations. The first and second instance judgments found facts clearly and applied the law correctly. The retrial request of China Railway 19th Bureau lacks factual and legal basis and should be dismissed.

This Court finds upon retrial that on May 29, 2012, Chongqing Construction Engineering Group and China Railway 19th Bureau signed an enforcement repayment agreement, and China Railway 19th Bureau has actually paid Chongqing Construction Engineering Group RMB 3,000,000. Other facts found by this Court upon retrial are consistent with those found in the second instance.

This Court holds that the subcontract signed by Chongqing Construction Engineering Group and China Railway 19th Bureau was approved by the project construction unit, Jinkai Company, and did not violate the mandatory provisions of laws or administrative regulations. It is legal and valid and is legally binding on both parties. Both parties shall perform in accordance with the agreement.

The focus of the dispute in this case is: how to determine the basis for settling the project funds between Chongqing Construction Engineering Group and China Railway 19th Bureau.

Regarding Chongqing Construction Engineering Group's assertion that the project in question falls within the scope of statutory audit and therefore must be settled based on the audit results of the state audit authority, this Court holds that according to the provisions and legislative intent of the Audit Law, the law provides that audit authorities shall conduct audit supervision over the budget implementation and final accounts of government-invested projects and projects mainly invested by the government, with the aim of maintaining the national financial and economic order, improving the efficiency of financial fund use, and preventing irregularities in construction projects. The settlement of project funds between Chongqing Construction Engineering Group and China Railway 19th Bureau belongs to the civil legal relationship between equal civil subjects. Therefore, the settlement of the disputed project funds in this case and the state audit provided by law in terms of subject, scope, and effect are legal relationships of different natures. That is, regardless of whether the project in question must be audited by a state audit authority according to law, it cannot be considered that the audit conclusions of the state audit authority can automatically become the basis for determining the settlement between the parties in this case. Therefore, this Court does not accept the above assertion of Chongqing Construction Engineering Group. The basis for settlement of the project in question shall be determined in accordance with the agreement and performance of the parties.

Regarding whether the subcontract stipulated that the project in question should be settled based on the audit conclusions of the state audit authority, this Court holds that the subcontract's provision that the final settlement price shall be subject to the proprietor's audit is because the contract is a subcontract. The final determination of the quantity and amount of the project requires reliance on the final confirmation of a third party outside the contract, i.e., the proprietor. Therefore, this provision should be interpreted to mean that the final settlement price must be determined through professional review channels or methods to ascertain the true reasonableness of the settled project funds, and the result must be approved by the proprietor. It should not be interpreted to mean that the settlement must be based on the audit results after the proprietor accepts the audit by the state audit authority. According to the Audit Law, the audit by the state audit authority is an administrative supervision act against the construction unit. The legal relationship between the auditor and the auditee arising from the state audit is different in nature from the civil legal relationship between the parties in this case. Therefore, in a civil contract, the parties' agreement to accept administrative audit as the basis for determining civil legal relations should be specific and clear, and cannot be inferred or presumed that the parties agreed at the time of contract formation to accept the intervention of state audit acts in the civil legal relationship. Therefore, Chongqing Construction Engineering Group's assertion that the subcontract provided for the use of the audit conclusions of the state audit authority as the settlement basis lacks factual and legal basis, and this Court does not accept it.

From the provisions of the subcontract and the performance of the contract by both parties, the project in question was completed on September 8, 2005, passed acceptance in December of the same year, and obtained the "Chongqing Construction Project Completion Acceptance Filing Registration Certificate" on February 6, 2006. Thereafter, for the purpose of providing a value basis for the completion settlement of the Lanfeng Tunnel and Huagou Tunnel sections of the road project, the EDZ Supervision and Audit Bureau commissioned Xiheng Company to conduct a completion settlement review of the above projects. On August 10, 2006, Xiheng Company issued a review report indicating that the project cost for the scope of the project in question was RMB 114,252,796. On December 5, 2007, Chongqing Construction Engineering Group and China Railway 19th Bureau settled the subcontract project, confirming that the settlement amount within the scope of China Railway 19th Bureau's drawings was RMB 114,252,795.85. Although during the first and second instance proceedings, the parties disputed whether the review report issued by Xiheng Company fell within the "proprietor's audit" agreed in the subcontract, on this review report, the proprietor, the contractor, and the subcontractor all signed and sealed to indicate their recognition of the review results. Subsequently, Chongqing Construction Engineering Group and China Railway 19th Bureau signed a settlement agreement, and the settlement amount determined therein was consistent with the amount determined in the above review report. This Court holds that the above facts can form a complete chain of evidence, proving that the settlement agreement signed by the parties on December 5, 2007, is a supplementary agreement intended to determine the final settlement price as agreed in the subcontract. Before the initiation of the lawsuit in this case, Chongqing Construction Engineering Group had cumulatively paid China Railway 19th Bureau RMB 98,120,156.63 for the project in question, which had reached 96% of the settlement amount agreed in the settlement agreement. The actual performance of the settlement agreement also corroborates that it represents the true intention of both parties. Although Chongqing Construction Engineering Group asserts that the settlement agreement was only a stage act in the settlement of the project funds in question, it did not provide corresponding evidence to prove this. Moreover, the subcontract did not require stage reviews and stage settlements of the project settlement, and the settlement agreement itself does not indicate that it is only a stage settlement of the project in question. Therefore, this Court does not accept the above assertion of Chongqing Construction Engineering Group. The settlement agreement is a legal and valid contract and is legally binding on both parties.

Considering the signing and actual performance of the settlement agreement, this Court holds that although during the trial of this case, the parties disputed whether the review report issued by Xiheng Company was the proprietor's audit agreed in the subcontract, that review report has been recognized by the proprietor of the project and both parties in this case. Moreover, Chongqing Construction Engineering Group and China Railway 19th Bureau signed a settlement agreement based on the review report and have already substantially performed it. Therefore, even if there is a difference between Xiheng Company's review report and the proprietor's audit agreed by the parties when signing the subcontract, according to Article 77, paragraph 1 of the Contract Law of the PRC, the parties' act of signing the settlement agreement and performing it can be regarded as a modification of the original settlement method agreed in the subcontract. This modification is legally binding on both parties. Where the parties have confirmed the settlement price of the project through a settlement agreement and have substantially performed it, an audit report issued by a state audit authority does not affect the validity of the settlement agreement. Now, Chongqing Construction Engineering Group proposes not to perform in accordance with the settlement agreement but has not provided corresponding evidence to prove that the agreement has defects in validity. Therefore, this Court does not support its assertion. China Railway 19th Bureau's claim for payment of arrears of project funds based on the above settlement agreement has factual and legal basis, and this Court supports it.

Regarding the interest claimed by China Railway 19th Bureau, this Court holds that neither the subcontract nor the settlement agreement clearly stipulated the time for payment of project funds, the standard of interest, or the time for calculation of interest. Therefore, whether interest on project funds should be paid and at what standard should be determined according to law. According to Articles 17 and 18 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Disputes over Construction Engineering Contracts, Chongqing Construction Engineering Group shall pay interest to China Railway 19th Bureau starting from the date of actual delivery of the project in question at the loan interest rate for the same period published by the People's Bank of China. The first and second instances did not ascertain the actual delivery date of the project in question. During the retrial, upon inquiry of both parties, neither could provide proof of the actual delivery time. Therefore, this Court, with reference to the above judicial interpretation, determines the starting date for calculating interest as the date when China Railway 19th Bureau filed its counterclaim.

Furthermore, regarding Chongqing Construction Engineering Group's assertion that the parties had signed an enforcement repayment agreement on May 29, 2012, and China Railway 19th Bureau had actually paid RMB 3,000,000, and therefore, according to judicial interpretation, the retrial review should be terminated, this Court holds that Article 25 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Trial Supervision Procedure of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC provides that a people's court may order termination of the review under the following circumstances, including paragraph (3): where the parties have reached a settlement agreement in enforcement and have performed it in full, unless the parties declare in the settlement agreement that they do not waive the right to apply for retrial. The applicable condition of the above judicial interpretation is that the parties have reached a settlement agreement and performed it in full. In this case, although China Railway 19th Bureau and Chongqing Construction Engineering Group reached a settlement agreement in enforcement, it has not been fully performed. Moreover, this judicial interpretation is directed at the review stage. In this case, the review stage has already ended, and the case has entered the retrial trial stage. Therefore, the above judicial interpretation should not apply, and this Court does not accept the above defense opinion of Chongqing Construction Engineering Group.

Additionally, regarding the calculation of case acceptance fees in this case, according to Article 18 of the Measures for the Payment of Litigation Fees, where a defendant files a counterclaim and the People's Court decides to hear them jointly, the case acceptance fee shall be reduced by half. The calculation of the second instance case acceptance fee in this case is incorrect, and this Court hereby corrects it.

In summary, this Court holds that the retrial request of China Railway 19th Bureau has factual and legal basis. The first and second instance judgments improperly determined the audit report of the Chongqing Municipal Audit Bureau as the settlement basis for the project in question between Chongqing Construction Engineering Group and China Railway 19th Bureau and should be corrected. Pursuant to Article 207, paragraph 1 and Article 170, paragraph 1, item (2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, this Court renders the following judgment:

1. Set aside the Chongqing High People's Court (2012) Yu Gao Fa Min Zhong Zi No. 00006 civil judgment;
2. Set aside the Chongqing No. 1 Intermediate People's Court (2010) Yu Yi Zhong Fa Min Chu Zi No. 425 civil judgment;
3. Within ten days after this judgment takes effect, Chongqing Construction Engineering Group Co., Ltd. shall pay China Railway 19th Bureau Group Co., Ltd. project funds of RMB 4,273,637.37, plus interest on the said project funds calculated from October 28, 2010 to the date of actual payment at the loan interest rate for the same period published by the People's Bank of China.

If the obligation to pay money is not performed within the period specified in this judgment, the debtor shall double the interest on the debt for the period of delayed performance in accordance with Article 253 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC.

The first instance case acceptance fee of RMB 32,729.80 and the first instance counterclaim case acceptance fee of RMB 20,495 shall be borne by Chongqing Construction Engineering Group Co., Ltd. The second instance case acceptance fee of RMB 53,224.80 shall be borne by Chongqing Construction Engineering Group Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.
